lectures.title: The Nature of Arguments
lectures.summary: The opening lecture of the six-part course. It teaches how to recognise arguments and what the nature of an argument is.

lectures.title: Different Types of Arguments
lectures.summary: The second of six lectures on critical reasoning, introducing the different types of arguments — in particular, deductive and inductive arguments.

lectures.title: Setting out Arguments Logic Book Style
lectures.summary: Part three of the series focuses on how to identify and analyse arguments, and how to set them out logic book-style to make them easier to evaluate.

lectures.title: What is a Good Argument? Validity and Truth
lectures.summary: Part four of the series turns to evaluating arguments and how to tell whether an argument is good or bad, focusing specifically on inductive arguments.

lectures.title: Evaluating Arguments Part One
lectures.summary: Part five continues with the evaluation of arguments — this time deductive arguments — focusing in particular on the notion of validity.

lectures.title: Evaluating Arguments Part Two
lectures.summary: In the final lecture the series looks at fallacies: bad arguments that can easily be mistaken for good arguments.

lectures.title: Further reading and more...
lectures.summary: A short closing item added after the course, pointing listeners who have finished the series of podcasts to where to go from here; not a teaching session.
